title: Source-first interpretation for a mechanical, human-piloted ornithopter

aspect_ratio.reading: The rounded 'Say' full span is 7.4 ft and the planform paragraph gives total area 6.61 ft^2 and AR=b^2/S.
aspect_ratio.excluded: The 3.135 ft wing-length conversion is internally inconsistent and is not used.

wrist_span_fraction.reading: Rounded wrist-to-wrist span 3.7 ft, full span 7.4 ft, explicitly annotated as 50% b.

photographs.readable_principle: Swan planform has a broad arm wing, rounded/tapered hand wing, and a wrist at half span. The area paragraph, not the inconsistent wing-length conversion, supplies aspect ratio.
photographs.implementation: A 14 m, AR 8.2844 planform with wrist fraction 0.5; source-mechanism generates the broad inner panel and four-segment rounded tapered outer outline.
photographs.uncertainty_or_assumption: The drawing is scaling evidence, not a construction drawing. Full-scale chord and area are calculated with the supplied 14 m span.

photographs.readable_principle: The photographed Göttingen curved-plate chart separates lift, drag and moment trends but has crowded axes and low-Re context.
photographs.implementation: Inner and outer local strip polars are interpolated from the supplied engineering tables; camber adds a separately stated lift increment.
photographs.uncertainty_or_assumption: No exact coefficients were digitised from this chart. The tables are favourable illustrative engineering completions, not Stanley's measurements.

photographs.readable_principle: Define a desired cyclic trajectory and compare candidate wing forces with its required vertical-force range; the stated objective is a powered man-carrying ornithopter.
photographs.implementation: The simulation computes local aerodynamic forces and the comparison panel may compare them with the sine-trajectory requirement; free flight is never prescribed to match it.
photographs.uncertainty_or_assumption: The notes provide a method, not a validated trajectory, engine, pilot mass, or full-scale design.

photographs.readable_principle: Straight and level flapping flight is necessarily cyclic in lift and thrust and therefore mildly undulating; recovery can reduce lift and leave a cyclic wake.
photographs.implementation: Strip forces vary naturally with crank phase, twist, local velocity and recovery overlap. COM motion remains dynamic rather than altitude-held.
photographs.uncertainty_or_assumption: Unsteady vortex rings and wake memory are omitted by the supplied reduced strip model.

photographs.readable_principle: At low speed the down/working stroke lasts longer than recovery; at cruise the periods become equal. Candidate lift and drag should be compared with required values, and wing/body elasticity may reduce inertial power.
photographs.implementation: theta=phi-b sin(phi), with fixed low-speed b=0.3 and cruise b=0; a real hinge spring, distributed wing inertia, drive inertia and aerodynamic work are coupled.
photographs.uncertainty_or_assumption: Handwritten marginal revisions are not treated as reliable numerical specifications. Timing and stiffness values are supplied engineering assumptions.

photographs.readable_principle: Wing/body mass-spring motion occurs about the common CG; fore/aft wing movement creates pitching reaction. Working hands move down/back while recovery trails and closes to reduce span and area.
photographs.implementation: The helper derives moving CG, inertia coupling B, application-point Jacobians and pitch moments from the same pose used for rendering. Outer leaves sweep, twist and overlap on recovery.
photographs.uncertainty_or_assumption: The sinusoidal linkage curves and two rigid sliding leaves explicitly complete prose that does not provide machine dimensions.

photographs.readable_principle: The opening continuation calls for reduced recovery area/span and adjusted local incidence. Camber, incidence and section shape are distinct; the later goshawk figure is only an example.
photographs.implementation: Exposure, twist and camber are independent pose fields and independent geometric/aerodynamic inputs.
photographs.uncertainty_or_assumption: The goshawk's printed 13/10/9/6 percent cambers are not assigned to the swan or aircraft.

photographs.readable_principle: The arm section is about 5–6% thick; the outer hand is a thin slotted curved plate whose high lift/drag is useful on the working stroke and reduced by trailing/closing on recovery. Conventional tail, rudder or weight shift are suitable completions.
photographs.implementation: Inner thickness metadata is 5.5%, outer 0.8%; curved overlapping leaves shorten exposed span on recovery. The aircraft has a conventional tailplane, elevator, fin and rudder.
photographs.uncertainty_or_assumption: Tail sizes, controls, local polars and mechanical structure are supplied completions, not notebook dimensions.

photographs.readable_principle: Glide work begins with D times V, while flapping adds induced, trajectory, acceleration and wing-inertia terms; ideal inertial exchange is not net energy production.
photographs.implementation: The model records shaft work, aerodynamic dissipation, transmission/damping heat and control work. The spring stores and returns energy while the finite 16 kW shaft is the only propulsion source.
photographs.uncertainty_or_assumption: The handwritten dimensional-analysis note is not used as a coefficient or performance claim.

engineering_completions: The supplied 55 kg seated pilot, 173.9 kg dry mass including pilot, 3.6 kg fuel and 177.5 kg initial wet mass are implemented.
The supplied 16 kW engine, governor, finite starting torque, transmission efficiency, spring, damping, mass allocation, tail and section tables fill absent quantities.
Outer geometry is represented by two rigid half-length leaves. Hidden overlap keeps its mass while exposed aerodynamic area changes.
The three-wheel ground model is a reduced rigid runway constraint, not suspension or tyre dynamics.
Section pitching moments, wake interaction, overlap-flow interference, flexible aeroelasticity and unsteady stall are omitted.
visual_interpretation: A triangulated metal/wood fuselage, visible engine and reduction crank, wishbone bearings and spring, broad fabric inner wings, overlapping curved hand-wing leaves, conventional tail, three pneumatic tyres and a helmeted seated adult make the mechanism and load paths legible. It translates the source principles rather than imitating a bird.
limitations: This is a favourable educational reduced model, not a recovered Stanley design, experimentally validated prediction, or buildable human-flight aircraft. Stanley is not claimed to have specified the engine, pilot, coefficient tables, masses, numerical linkage curves or controls.
